transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-07 09:13 UTC; Duration 56m; Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Chopra (Growth), Alex Morgan (Catalyst Events), Jules T. (Catalyst Prod).

Summary auto-generated (may be rough): finalize webinar runbook and promotional sprint, assign owners, agree registration KPI and rehearsal schedule.

[00:00:00] Lena Park: All right good morning everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick check — is everybody seeing the agenda I just dropped?
[00:00:08] Alex Morgan: Yep seeing it. Sorry, slight lag, I'm on mobile but looks good.
[00:00:12] Priya Chopra: Cool, we'll run through 6-week promo and then the speaker runbook. Lena, Marco you good to kick off?
[00:00:20] Lena Park: Yup - I'll do quick context then Marco will talk demo requirements and fallback.
[00:00:27] Marco Ruiz: Hey, hi all. A couple things — there are a few demo-specific constraints, like the K-V cache prewarm we do for long context tests, and our live infra needs a warmed endpoint, otherwise you see a 200-400ms bump.
[00:00:45] Jules T.: Sorry, what did you say? K-V what? I think the transcript later reads K-V cash, so just flagging.
[00:00:51] Marco Ruiz: K-V cache, kv cache. Yeah, sorry, tech lingo.
[00:00:55] Lena Park: High level: marketing objective is product-led growth motion — hunt PSGs and infra platform teams with a practical demo of latency/cost tradeoffs. Target audience: infra/platform eng leads at mid-market SaaS.
[00:01:10] Alex Morgan: And timeline? You were aiming to run this late October, right?
[00:01:14] Priya Chopra: Yes target week of Oct 27, ideally Thursday. We have a 6-week promo sprint from Oct 13 to Nov 24 — though last promo touches will be 2 days pre-event.
[00:01:25] Lena Park: Decision items: format length, speakers, promo channels, registration target, and rehearsal cadence.
[00:01:31] Alex Morgan: Ok quick preference — 45 minutes feels right: 20 demo, 15 case study/customer, 10 live Q&A. Keep it tight.
[00:01:40] Marco Ruiz: That works — for the 20-min demo we need 10 minutes for the live demo, 5 for quick architecture slide, and 5 for a short benchmark / cost chart walkthrough. If we go live, we need a fallback recording if infra hiccups.
[00:01:55] Priya Chopra: Noted. We'll include a fallback video. Who's the customer case study? Lena?
[00:02:01] Lena Park: We're lining up a customer intro — tentative: Solstice Health (they're internal). If that falls we can use a prerecorded case study.
[00:02:07] Alex Morgan: On promo — recommend paid LinkedIn Sponsored Content, 2 partner newsletters, and a small X/Twitter ad spend as a brand touch. Organic across Redwood channels, and we can push into partner channels.
[00:02:20] Priya Chopra: Agreed. Also piloting a gated checklist download tied to registration — will require a landing page + UTM tracking.
[00:02:28] Jules T.: Platform wise — what are you using? Hopin? Zoom Webinar? Will you need breakout rooms?
[00:02:33] Alex Morgan: We usually recommend Zoom Webinar for scale, Hopin if you want expo rooms. For this, Zoom Webinar + branded Q&A should be fine. We'll provision a practice room for rehearsals.
[00:02:44] Marco Ruiz: Zoom Webinar is fine, but I need RTP/port details for the demo machine and permission whitelisting for the endpoint — if it's on a VPC we need IP allowlisting.
[00:02:56] Lena Park: Good call. Action: Alex to confirm platform and share access details.
[00:03:02] Alex Morgan: Yep will do.
[00:03:04] [00:03:30] Lena Park: Registration goal — what's realistic? Priya?
[00:03:34] Priya Chopra: Benchmarks: For mid-market vertical, we can aim 1,200 registrations, 18% attendance (so ~216 live attendees), and 18% of attendees converting to MQLs — that yields ~39 MQLs. These are aggressive but with paid partner promos doable.
[00:03:50] Alex Morgan: 1,200 seems achievable with two partner newsletters + sponsored. Budget?
[00:03:55] Priya Chopra: Budget ask about $6-8k for paid ads and partner amplification fees. We'll tighten by channel once we run the audience lists.
[00:04:05] Marco Ruiz: Question on registration form fields — we need to capture cloud provider, team size, primary use case, and also a checkbox for allow follow-up. For compliance we shouldn't capture sensitive PII beyond email.
[00:04:18] Lena Park: Add SSO options? Not on the reg form, but post-webinar gating can link to SSO-enabled demos.
[00:04:25] Priya Chopra: Tracking: use UTM on all channels, register through Marketo form, and tie to Salesforce campaign. Alex to ensure platform passes UTM data.
[00:04:34] Alex Morgan: Yep we'll map utm_source/medium/campaign to the reg form.
[00:04:39] [00:05:00] Priya Chopra: Next the speaker runbook — this is important for consistency. I have a draft but want input: 3 slides for intro and housekeeping, 4 slides for architecture, 3 slides for demo context and dataset, 6 slides for live demo screenshots + steps, 2 slides for cost/throughput comparison, 2 slides for customer story, 1 slide for CTA and resources. Keep total deck under 20 slides.
[00:05:20] Marco Ruiz: For demo we need a consistent seed prompt, short deterministic prompt set, and a warmup sequence so the KV cache has entries. Also need to limit tokens to avoid throttling on shared endpoints. I can provide a 90-second demo script.
[00:05:36] Lena Park: Marco will own the demo script and fallback video. Priya will own deck checklist and slide counts. Alex will own platform and rehearsal schedule.
[00:05:45] Jules T.: A note on accessibility — can we get captions and a transcript auto-export? Some partners insist on captioning.
[00:05:51] Alex Morgan: Zoom auto-captions are OK but we can provide a cleaned transcript post-event. I'll include closed captions.
[00:05:57] [00:06:30] Priya Chopra: Promo calendar — week -2 to event: paid pushes, organic social, email sequence to Redwood lists (3 touches), partner newsletters (one blast T-10 days, one reminder T-2 days). We'll also open registration with a gated checklist incentive. On day-of pre-event reminder at 2 hours and 30 minutes.
[00:06:51] Lena Park: Who does the copy? Priya does primary, but need approvals from product and legal for any claims re performance.
[00:06:59] Priya Chopra: I'll draft copy and route for product approval by Oct 9.
[00:07:04] Marco Ruiz: On the technical side, any claims like "2x cost reduction" need benchmark notes. We should include a small methods slide.
[00:07:12] Lena Park: Yes add a methods/assumptions footnote.
[00:07:16] Alex Morgan: For partner amplification, we can offer co-branded landing pages for top partners — that usually increases conversions by 12-15%.
[00:07:25] Priya Chopra: Let's plan one co-branded landing page for Router Partners.
[00:07:29] [00:07:55] Lena Park: Rehearsal schedule — two rehearsals: technical dry run T-7 days and full dress T-2 days. Marco and customer to attend T-7. Full dress with speaker and production team T-2.
[00:08:05] Alex Morgan: We'll reserve 60 minutes for the T-7 and 90 for the T-2.
[00:08:10] Priya Chopra: Who's the moderator? Lena?
[00:08:13] Lena Park: I can moderate but would like Alexis (CSM) to be backup. I'll confirm.
[00:08:20] [00:08:50] Marco Ruiz: Demo specifics — plan A: live run against dedicated staging (best), plan B: live run against hosted API with prewarmed cache, plan C: play fallback video. Need to test for cold start and long context token growth.
[00:09:05] Jules T.: Can you briefly explain cold start and kv so the non-technical attendees understand?
[00:09:10] Marco Ruiz: Sure — cold start means the first token can take longer because the model weights haven't been moved into GPU memory; KV cache is key-value memory from prior tokens to speed continuing contexts. In transcript it sometimes becomes K-V cash which is cute but wrong.
[00:09:25] [00:09:40] Alex Morgan: Marketing asks — open to sponsorship? We have one small sponsorship slot with partners; might be a small logo placement in exchange for promotional lift.
[00:09:48] Priya Chopra: Fine as long as sponsor isn't a direct competitor. No Anthropic or OpenAI sponsored content.
[00:09:55] Lena Park: Competitor policy reiterated: no competing model vendors. Keep partners infra/tooling.
[00:09:59] [00:10:30] Priya Chopra: Measurement - registrations, attendance rate, Q&A volume, demo drop-off time, CTA clicks (request demo / trial), and post-event MQL conversion. We'll instrument tracking via SFDC campaign and Marketo. Need UTM discipline.
[00:10:44] Marco Ruiz: Also metric: demo latency numbers and a simple cost/token chart. I'll provide a CSV of benchmark numbers that Priya can screenshot for slides.
[00:10:55] Alex Morgan: For the registration landing page, can we have a two-column layout: left for event copy and CTA, right for checklist / resources preview? We can provide a template.
[00:11:06] Priya Chopra: Yes, template helpful. Alex, send template by Oct 8.
[00:11:10] [00:11:40] Jules T.: One production note — please avoid long code blocks during screenshare, the video compression makes them unreadable.
[00:11:46] Marco Ruiz: Agreed, we'll show high-level architecture and then zoom in on small screenshots for code snippets.
[00:11:54] Lena Park: Good. Now risks: customer no-shows, demo fails, registration underperformance. Mitigations: pre-event reminder cadence, fallback video, partner promo contingency, and a paid boost if registration falls below 600 by T-10 days.
[00:12:13] Priya Chopra: Also add a nurture track post-event for no-shows.
[00:12:17] [00:12:50] Alex Morgan: Logistics — who uploads the deck and where? We recommend a shared Google Drive folder; production will pull the final PPT 24 hours before event.
[00:12:58] Lena Park: I'll create the folder and invite team.
[00:13:02] Priya Chopra: Slide deck naming convention: EventDate_Company_Webinar_V1. We'll iterate.
[00:13:08] [00:13:35] Marco Ruiz: Quick note about recording: if we play a fallback recording, we need clear labeling to the audience so no claims about live that are misleading. Also need to ensure the recording has captions.
[00:13:48] Alex Morgan: We'll flag recorded segments as "pre-recorded demo" in agenda.
[00:13:52] [00:14:20] Priya Chopra: Creative assets: social graphics (3 sizes), email banners (600x200), hero images, co-branded logos, and a one-pager lead gen PDF. Who needs final source files?
[00:14:29] Lena Park: I'll own source files consolidation. Priya design team to create assets. Alex to provide partner logos.
[00:14:35] [00:14:58] Alex Morgan: On legal/compliance: any claims re customer names need permission. For Solstice Health we need sign-off to use them as a case study.
[00:15:06] Lena Park: I'll follow up with customer success to secure release by Oct 15.
[00:15:11] [00:15:40] Priya Chopra: Email sequence — three touches: T-14 announcement, T-3 reminder with co-host highlight, and T-1 day last call. Also segment lists by persona and send slightly different copy for infra vs product leads.
[00:15:58] Marco Ruiz: For the demo script I'll include two branches: if the dedicated host is up, show live perf; if not, play pre-recorded. I'll also include a safety cue to switch to the recording.
[00:16:12] Alex Morgan: We need a communication plan for last-minute outages — prod to email registrants 30 minutes in advance if we change modality.
[00:16:22] Lena Park: Good.
[00:16:45] [00:17:10] Priya Chopra: Promo copy draft idea: "Serving LLMs at scale: balancing latency, cost, and reliability — a hands-on demo and customer playbook." Short subject line for email: "How Redwood reduces inference costs — live demo". Any objections?
[00:17:26] Marco Ruiz: Avoid saying "reduces costs by X" unless we have benchmark footnote. Use "cost-efficient" language.
[00:17:33] Priya Chopra: Will update copy.
[00:17:40] [00:18:05] Lena Park: Ok let's go through final owners and due dates quickly. Priya will share promo calendar by Oct 9, Marco demo/fallback by Oct 14, Alex platform details by Oct 12, Lena to secure customer permission by Oct 15. Any additions?
[00:18:20] Alex Morgan: I'll also send rehearsal calendar.
[00:18:24] Priya Chopra: I'll set up the Marketo campaign and invite Redwood to the asset folder.
[00:18:30] [00:19:00] Jules T.: Small detail — what is the CTA post-event? Book a dedicated cost review? Request trial?
[00:19:06] Lena Park: Primary CTA: Request a dedicated pilot / trial. Secondary: download the playbook checklist.
[00:19:12] Priya Chopra: We'll use two CTAs and track both as separate events.
[00:19:17] [00:19:50] Alex Morgan: For speakers — we need short bios (40–60 words) and headshots. Deadline: Oct 15.
[00:19:58] Lena Park: I'll collect bios from speakers and forward to Priya.
[00:20:05] [00:20:35] Priya Chopra: Any thought on offering an incentive — raffle for attendees — e.g., $100 gift cards for 5 attendees? That can bump attendance rate.
[00:20:45] Marco Ruiz: Works. Ensure legal ok with raffle.
[00:20:48] Alex Morgan: We'll include a slide mentioning raffle rules.
[00:20:53] [00:21:20] Lena Park: Great. Slight tangent — can we do a quick run of the landing page copy skeleton?
[00:21:26] Priya Chopra: Headline, subhead, 3 bullets on what you'll learn, CTA, speaker strip, customer logos, and resource preview. Keep form minimal.
[00:21:38] Alex Morgan: Send me the copy and I'll mock in the template.
[00:21:43] [00:22:10] Priya Chopra: Ok, anything else?
[00:22:15] Jules T.: Just one more production note — test audio levels across speakers before full dress. We usually do that T-2.
[00:22:21] Alex Morgan: Agreed.
[00:22:25] Lena Park: All right let's recap and close.
[00:22:30] [00:22:55] Lena Park: Recap: 45-minute format, registration target 1,200, playbook and checklist incentive, Zoom Webinar chosen, rehearsal T-7 and T-2, action owners: Priya (promo), Marco (demo), Alex (platform & rehearsals), Lena (customer permission + moderation).
[00:23:10] Priya Chopra: I'll circulate the promo calendar and a one-page runbook by Oct 9.
[00:23:16] Marco Ruiz: I'll finalize demo script and fallback by Oct 14 and share test vectors.
[00:23:22] Alex Morgan: I'll lock the platform, send access, and the rehearsal times by Oct 12.
[00:23:28] Lena Park: Great. There were a few sidebar notes and crosstalk but those are the main items.
[00:23:35] [00:24:00] Speaker 1: Uh small Q — will we record the MQL funnel?
[00:24:05] Priya Chopra: Yes we'll report post-event funnel metrics in the campaign dashboard — registrations -> attendance -> CTA clicks -> MQLs.
[00:24:12] [00:24:40] Alex Morgan: I'll also provide production notes and the rehearsal access.
[00:24:46] Lena Park: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email. End.

(Transcription notes: occasional mis-attributed lines, some technical terms transcribed imperfectly, e.g., K-V cache become K-V cash or KV-cash. Natural speech with brief interruptions and filler words.)
